note: Bounded areas candidate discovery can survey. A raw area must lie inside the loaded road-network extract and the loaded habitat extracts; discovery reports PARTIAL coverage rather than guessing when it does not. A derived-first area (derivedOnly) names a discovery catalog whose plane carries its own coverage, so it declares no raw-extract requirements.

publishedRegion.name: Greater Portland region (Oregon and south-west Washington)
publishedRegion.note: The published regional coverage the derived corridor-metrics plane covers. It is declared here so the interface can classify a search centre as FULL, PARTIAL or NONE before any data is fetched; tests/discovery.test.js asserts it still equals the bounds of published regional/manifest.json and of the derived manifest, which are the authorities.

discoveryRegion.name: Conterminous United States
discoveryRegion.note: The coverage the production discovery catalog declares: the published region of the national derived plane (data/national/derived-catalog.json), which a test asserts agree. A derived-first search is classified against it, so a centre anywhere in the conterminous United States is runnable. publishedRegion above stays the window the committed Oregon raw material and the place gazetteer were built for.

searchAreas.name: Oregon pilot area
searchAreas.note: The same bounded window the road, wetland, hydrography, and ecoregion extracts were built for: about 25 km by 18 km west of Portland, Oregon, in Washington and Multnomah counties.

searchAreas.name: Portland west region (partitioned)
searchAreas.note: A real larger Oregon test area within the partitioned TIGER, NWI and NHD coverage; local data files are served through the same static manifest contract as future R2 objects.

searchAreas.name: Regional benchmark: 10-mile radius
searchAreas.note: Committed benchmark scenario on a fixed centre, so 10-, 25- and 50-mile searches differ only in radius. The bounding box selects cells; the disk decides which corridors are inside the search.

searchAreas.name: Regional benchmark: 25-mile radius
searchAreas.note: Committed benchmark scenario: one 25-mile radius disk on the same fixed centre as the 10- and 50-mile cases.

searchAreas.name: Regional benchmark: 50-mile radius
searchAreas.note: Committed benchmark scenario: one 50-mile radius disk on the same fixed centre, inside the published Greater Portland region with room for its 1 km habitat halo and cross-cell road continuity.

searchAreas.name: National derived: 10-mile radius
searchAreas.note: The interactive search template production discovery uses: a centre and radius anywhere in the conterminous United States, resolved through data/national/derived-catalog.json. It is derivedOnly - the national derived corridor-metrics plane is the discovery payload, and it carries its own published coverage - so it declares no raw-extract requirements. Keeping it last leaves the committed 10/25/50-mile benchmark scenarios, and their declared order, exactly as they were.
